Dear Karl

I have the same question, as already posted in 2009 by the user "Masato". I placed Masato's question as well as your answer from that time bellow.

Thus my question now is: "Has anything changed since 2009 and today, thus is your today's answer the same or a different one?"

Many thanks for your help.

Mark



User "Masato" Question 04/03/2009:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hello, 

I wonder if I can perform the permutation test of multiple qtl model. 
When I scanned the genome with scanone and scantwo, I could not get 
any peak over the threshold level (alpha=0.05)  according to my 
permutation-test (I used cluster for scantwo.perm). 
I picked up a couple of highest peaks which were even blow alpha=0.10, 
and builded a multiple qtl model, perform fitqtl, addqtl, addpair, 
etc. to refined it. 
Then I have got a 8QTLs with 3 interactions model. Each QTL and 
interaction are highly significant according to p-value . 
My wondering point is whether I can conclude they are "real QTLs" 
because I couldn't get any significant peak in my scanone and scantwo 
results. 
I am hoping I could get the LOD threshold info of alpha=0.05 which I 
can apply the result of fitqtl. 

The following may not make any sense, but just in the case if it 
works. 
addcovar and intcovar options in scanone and scantwo seem useful if I 
perform permutation tests on each chromosome separately, but I'm not 
sure if I can incorporate the epistasis between QTLs outside of the 
chromosome I'm scanning. 
(my model is y~Q1*Q3+Q2+Q4+Q5*Q6+Q7*Q8. All QTLs are on different 
chromosomes. How I can write in addcovar and intcovar when I perform 
permutation test on Q2?, and others?) 

Or, if there is a better way to think, I really appreciate it if you 
would let me know. 
Thank you. 

Best, 
Masato
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------



Karl answer 05/03/2009
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The p-values provided by fitqtl() are pointwise, and do not adjust for 
any genome-scan used to identify the putative QTL. 

There is no simple way to use a permutation test in the context of a 
multiple-QTL model, particularly in the presence of epistatic 
interactions. 

addcovar and intcovar in scanone and scantwo concern environmental 
covariates and QTL x covariate interactions, respectively. 

karl
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
